Review any check: notes where a resource could not be narrowed from configuration. Custom adapters should declare access explicitly as well.

Check release support

Use the release scope when planning a feature. It records supported behavior, its test coverage, operational limits, and planned capabilities. The specification describes the target design, and architecture decisions explain the choices behind the implementation.

Contribute to the library itself

Use this workflow for changes to shared library behavior. Run it from the library checkout:

cd /d "%LIBRARY%"
"%PYTHON%" tools/install_dev.py
"%PYTHON%" -m pytest
"%PYTHON%" -m ruff check .
"%PYTHON%" -m ruff format --check .
"%PYTHON%" -m mypy
"%PYTHON%" -c "from importlinter.cli import lint_imports; lint_imports()"

On macOS/Linux, use cd "$LIBRARY" for the first line and "$PYTHON" for the Python commands. The installation helper uses pip. Import-linter checks that code respects the package dependency boundaries.

For changes to Agent Lab, use its isolated package launcher and UI checks. The library's default test command does not replace that suite. The code map shows which package owns each responsibility.

Keep a change in the layer that owns it. Put shared interfaces in contracts, provider-specific behavior in adapters, and LangGraph behavior in its integration. Add a regression test that fails before the fix. For a new adapter, run its contract tests; for a template change, test a freshly generated consumer.

Keep code and its documentation consistent

Reuse existing interfaces where they fit. Introduce an abstraction when it separates a responsibility or makes a dependency replaceable in tests. Use the following package boundaries to decide where the change belongs.

LocationWhat belongs there
core/contracts/Shared value objects, errors, and protocols that describe the operations implementations provide.
core/config/Read and validate settings once. Pass resolved values to other layers.
core/di/Select factories, resolve declared dependencies, and own adapter startup and cleanup.
core/pipeline/Governed-call rules expressed through framework-neutral protocols.
core/adapters/ and ai_agent_lib_aws/ Implement protocols using files, APIs, databases, or provider SDKs.
core/integrations/Translate between library contracts and HTTP, MCP, or LangGraph types and lifecycle behavior.
ai_agent_lib_cli/Read generation inputs, render templates, and write projects. Keep CLI parsing separate from generation logic.
core/testing/Reusable fakes and contract suites. A contract suite checks behavior that every implementation must preserve.

In this table, core/ means packages/ai-agent-lib-core/src/ai_agent_lib_core/. The AWS and CLI packages have their own matching packages/<distribution>/src/ directories.

Name things by their role

  • Use snake_case for modules, functions, methods, and variables; PascalCase for classes; and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants. Prefix internal helpers with _. Keep established public names stable, including exceptions such as PolicyDenied.
  • A port describes a role, such as AuditSink. An adapter implements it. A provider name selects a factory in configuration. ProviderSpec is the factory definition; the container holds the live instance.
  • Use established suffixes when they help: Options for validated adapter settings, Interceptor for a pipeline stage, Bindings for integration assembly, and Answers for CLI generation inputs. Name functions for the action they perform.
  • Keep external and Python names distinct. The service claims-mcp uses the package claims_mcp and defaults to the registry ID claims. A model alias such as default is separate from a provider name such as anthropic and the provider's model ID.
  • Use request_id for correlation, thread_id for a conversation, and invocation_id for one invocation's budget. Keep these identifiers distinct in data models and logs.

Document the contract and the reason

Start a module docstring with its responsibility and boundaries. Start a class docstring with its role, and document constructor arguments there. For a public function, explain what the caller must provide and can rely on. Use the existing Google-style Args:, Returns:, Raises:, and Attributes: sections when they add useful detail; a clear one-line docstring is enough for a simple accessor.

For resources, explain who creates and closes them. For async work, explain cancellation, cleanup, and side effects. For example, entering a ServiceContainer builds adapters; validate() is an explicit readiness step. Describe which checks occur before execution and which occur after an operation may have produced side effects.

Use comments for decisions that the code alone does not explain, such as why cleanup must run in the task that created a resource. Avoid comments that merely restate an assignment. Keep the full caller contract at the public entry point; an internal collaborator can refer to it and explain only its own responsibility. When a behavior changes, update its docstring, regression test, generated template, and example together where applicable.

Ruff checks naming and Google-style docstrings, mypy checks types, and Import-linter checks dependencies. Review documented guarantees against failure paths as well as the successful path. Keep executable examples complete, and distinguish tests using permissive fakes from tests of real policy and registry configuration.

To edit this guide, change docs/guide/guide.src.html, then regenerate and check the output:

"%PYTHON%" docs/guide/build_guide.py
"%PYTHON%" docs/guide/build_guide.py --check
"%PYTHON%" -m pytest tests/architecture/test_generated_docs.py

Commit the source and docs/developer-guide.html together. Variable names, defaults, adapter options, and API tables below come from code. The local and AWS examples live in docs/guide/configuration_examples.py; tests check their coverage and adapter options. Update these sources and regenerate rather than manually editing the generated HTML.

Look up a setting or command

The environment, profile, adapter, option, CLI, extras, and public-export tables are generated from this checkout. Expand the group you need, or use your browser's Find command.

Configuration variables: local and AWS

This is the complete list of environment variables bound by ai-agent-lib, followed by OpenTelemetry, Python/pip setup and rmprep context settings used in this guide. Local means the Windows tutorial. AWS means the team's Fargate deployment. Values are examples unless labelled as defaults; replace service names, endpoints, IDs, and paths with values supplied by your team. Set only the variables your service needs.

How the settings fit the AWS design

Run agents and MCP servers as ECS Fargate services. The generated deployment runs OPA as a sidecar in each service's task; a separate OPA service is also possible through the policy URL. The future frontend signs users in with Microsoft Entra ID. Each backend verifies an access token issued for its API; an agent obtains a downstream MCP token using Entra's on-behalf-of flow. The local static identity supplies test subjects, tenants, and roles through configuration instead. See identity setup for API registrations, roles, scopes, and audiences.

  • Business data: MCP tools use named queries against the existing curated Redshift tables through the Redshift Data API. The upstream data lake remains outside this application.
  • Operational data: use managed PostgreSQL for checkpoints and the team's registry and role/resource mapping tables. The current postgres adapter implements checkpoints only. RDS for PostgreSQL and Aurora PostgreSQL support IAM database authentication; RDS Proxy with IAM is an optional connection-pooling layer. Registry tables need a new provider or a publishing job that produces the current S3 registry format. Mapping tables need an integration that supplies policy data, such as OPA data bundles. No environment variable creates these integrations. Keep their schemas and migrations separate from the library's checkpoint tables.
  • Logs in S3: the audit provider sends records to Firehose; configure an S3 destination on that stream. The generated Fargate template sends container logs to CloudWatch Logs. To archive agent, MCP, and OPA logs in S3, add a delivery route such as FireLens to Firehose. Diagnostic model traces need a collector that reads their file. S3 delivery for container logs and diagnostic files is additional infrastructure; the generated template does not configure it.
  • Files in S3: use S3 objects for durable documents, exports, and registry snapshots. File-path options still mean paths inside the container; setting them to s3://... does not add S3 access. Package static SQL and policy files in images, or arrange a download before startup. Use temporary task storage for scratch files. If an application needs a shared filesystem with file operations, EFS is a supported Fargate option; it requires a volume configuration. The library has no general filesystem provider or automatic S3 upload for application files.

Fargate CPU, memory, images, networking, task roles, databases, log delivery, S3 retention, and OPA bundle distribution are infrastructure settings. The deployment team configures them through the generated Terraform files and platform services; they are not additional EAP_ variables.

Where to put a value

For library settings, edit the service's .env locally. For AWS, put non-secret settings in the service's .env.aws used by the deployment generator; it writes them into the task environment. Use Secrets Manager for runtime secrets. Restart a service after changing its settings. Unknown EAP_ names and unknown JSON option keys stop startup.

The OTEL_ and PIP_ rows are owned by their SDK/tool: set them in the process environment (or the tool's supported configuration), not just in a service's .env. The library reads .env without changing the process environment. In Command Prompt, for example:

set "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318"

The SDK exposes additional tuning settings beyond those used here; consult OpenTelemetry configuration and pip configuration when your platform team needs them. In JSON, use forward slashes in paths (as below) or escape each Windows backslash as \\. Local registry and policy examples assume a service under agents/helper or mcps/directory; retain the paths generated for your service. Follow each adapter link for every accepted JSON field and its default. Scroll within the table vertically or horizontally to see more rows and columns. You can also focus it with Tab and use the arrow keys.

API key for the optional Anthropic exampleUnset with BedrockThe env secrets provider accepts this name or EAP_SECRET_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; set only one. With Secrets Manager, store the value as <prefix>anthropic_api_key instead.

Options such as auth_secret name the secret, never its value. Keep values out of source control and images.

The library uses OTLP over HTTP, not gRPC. S3 is not an OTLP endpoint.

Adapter options

Accepted keys for each adapter's JSON options. Data-source options sit beside "kind" in EAP_DATA_SOURCES. Unknown keys are rejected.

model Â· anthropic

Anthropic prompt caching; every call still runs the model pipeline. (AnthropicModelOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
prompt_cachingtrue | falsefalse
cache_ttl"5m" | "1h"5m

model Â· bedrock

No options. Uses the AWS session settings (AWS_PROFILE, AWS_REGION) and EAP_TLS_CA_BUNDLE.

model Â· fake local only

No options. Echoes the question as fake: <question>; tests script its replies.

secrets Â· env

No options. Serves each secret from a EAP_SECRET_<NAME> variable.

secrets Â· secrets_manager

Options of the secrets_manager secrets provider. (SecretsManagerOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
prefixtext""Put before a secret's name to form its ID in Secrets Manager, for example eap/accounts-agent/. It keeps one service's secrets apart from another's, and an IAM policy can be scoped to it.
cache_secondsnumber300.0How long a secret is kept before it is read again, so that a rotated secret is picked up without a restart. 0 reads it every time.

audit Â· firehose

Options of the firehose audit sink. (FirehoseAuditOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
tracingtrue | falsefalseAlso emit metadata-only OpenTelemetry events and metrics.
streamtextrequiredThe name of the Firehose stream that receives the records.

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
tracingtrue | falsefalseAlso emit metadata-only OpenTelemetry events and metrics.
pathpath.agentlib/audit.jsonlThe file to append to. Parent directories are created.
fsynctrue | falsetrueForce each record to disk before write returns.

identity Â· jwt

Options of the jwt identity provider. (JwtIdentityOptions)

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
preset"entra"not setentra fills in the issuer, key location, token endpoint and claim names for Microsoft Entra ID from tenant_id.
tenant_idtextnot setThe Entra tenant (directory) ID.
token_version1 | 22The version of access token this application is registered to receive from Entra.
authoritytexthttps://login.microsoftonline.comThe Entra sign-in host, for national clouds.
issuertextnot setThe exact iss value to accept. Required without a preset.
jwks_urltextnot setWhere the issuer publishes its signing keys. Required without a preset.
audiencetext | list of textrequiredThe aud value or values that identify this service.
algorithmslist of "RS256" | "RS384" | "RS512" | "PS256" | "PS384" | "PS512" | "ES256" | "ES384" | "ES512" | "EdDSA"["RS256"]The signature algorithms to accept. Only asymmetric ones exist here.
claimsobject of text{}Claim names that differ from the preset, by what they supply: subject, tenant, roles, actor, scopes, kind.
tenanttextnot setThe tenant every caller belongs to, when tokens carry no tenant claim.
required_scopeslist of text[]Delegated scopes a user's token must all carry.
accept_service_tokenstrue | falsefalseAccept tokens an application obtained for itself, with no user. Refused unless this is set.
service_tokens_are"kind_claim" | "without_scopes" | "actor_is_subject"not setHow an application's own token is told from a user's. Required without a preset, because issuers differ and a wrong guess would let an application act as a user.
service_kindslist of text["app"]The values of the kind claim that mark an application's own token, for kind_claim.
leeway_secondsinteger60Clock difference tolerated when checking validity.
jwks_cache_secondsinteger86400How long the signing keys are kept before they are read again.
timeout_secondsnumber5.0How long reading the signing keys may take.
ca_filepathnot setA CA file for the identity provider, when it is signed by a private authority.
use_proxytrue | falsefalseReach the identity provider through the platform's outbound proxy.
allow_httptrue | falsefalseAllow URLs without TLS on a host other than this machine.
exchangeobjectkeys belowHow to obtain tokens for the services this one calls. An MCP server that calls nothing else leaves it out.
exchange.kind"on_behalf_of" | "token_exchange"not seton_behalf_of is the JWT bearer grant as Microsoft Entra ID implements delegation. token_exchange is RFC 8693. The default follows the preset.
exchange.client_idtextrequiredThis service's own identifier at the identity provider.
exchange.client_secrettextoauth_client_secretThe name of the secret that holds this service's client secret.
exchange.token_urltextnot setThe token endpoint. The preset supplies it.
exchange.scopetextnot setThe scope to ask for, where {audience} stands for the audience of the service being called.
exchange.timeout_secondsnumber10.0How long one exchange may take.

OptionTypeDefaultMeaning
subjecttextdev-userThe subject a caller without a development token is treated as.
tenanttextdev-tenantThe tenant such a caller is treated as belonging to.
roleslist of text[]The roles such a caller is given.
audiencetextnot setThe name this service accepts development tokens for. Without it a token for any audience is accepted.
token_ttl_secondsinteger300How long a development token is valid.

CLI commands and flags

The command names below use agentlib as shorthand. In Command Prompt, run them with "%PYTHON%" -m ai_agent_lib_cli; in bash/zsh use "$PYTHON" -m ai_agent_lib_cli. Add --help to any command to list its accepted flags.

agentlib check

Run what CI runs: lint, format, types, tests and the policy samples.

agentlib check [OPTIONS]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--opaoffAlso check that OPA agrees with the rules.
--keep-goingoffRun every check even after one fails.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib config explain

Show every setting of SERVICE and where it came from. Secrets are masked.

agentlib config explain [OPTIONS] SERVICE
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib config options

List the adapters of each PORT, or the options of the adapter NAME with their defaults.

agentlib config options [OPTIONS] [PORT] [NAME]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--schemaoffPrint the adapter's options as JSON Schema, for an editor.

agentlib deploy

Write the Terraform and Dockerfiles that run SERVICE on ECS Fargate.

agentlib deploy [OPTIONS] SERVICE
FlagDefaultMeaning
--planoffShow what would be deployed and why; write nothing.
--bundlenoneThe platform's Rego bundle, for the OPA sidecar. Default: the library checkout's.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib doctor

Check what the workspace, or one SERVICE, needs in order to run.

agentlib doctor [OPTIONS] [SERVICE]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--no-pinsoffDo not start each MCP server to compare its pins.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib eval

Run the evals of SERVICE, or of every service: its tests marked eval, with a real model.

agentlib eval [OPTIONS] [SERVICE]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--acceptoffAfter the evals pass, save the report as the service's evals/baseline.json.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib graph

Print the graph of AGENT as a Mermaid diagram.

agentlib graph [OPTIONS] AGENT
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib init

Create a workspace folder called NAME.

agentlib init [OPTIONS] [NAME]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--dir.Where to create the workspace folder. Default: the current folder.
--ownernoneThe team that owns the workspace.
--lib-pathnoneA local checkout of ai-agent-lib to install the library from.
--lib-versionnoneInstall the library from a package index, e.g. '>=0.1'.
--answersnoneGenerate the workspace an agentlib.toml describes, services included.
--forceoffOverwrite files that exist and differ.

agentlib install

Install every workspace service and its dependencies with Python's pip.

agentlib install [OPTIONS]
FlagDefaultMeaning
--no-devoffOmit the workspace's development tools.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib link

Let AGENT call the tools of the MCP server SERVER.

agentlib link [OPTIONS] AGENT SERVER
FlagDefaultMeaning
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib new agent

Add a hello-world LangGraph agent called NAME, with its tests.

agentlib new agent [OPTIONS] NAME
FlagDefaultMeaning
--descriptionnoneOne line on what the agent does.
--modelnoneThe model provider. 'fake' needs no account. Default: fake.
--mcpnoneAn MCP server the agent may call. Repeatable.
--portnoneLocal HTTP port.
--forceoffOverwrite files that exist and differ.
--workspacenoneA folder inside the workspace. Default: the current folder.

agentlib new mcp

Add an MCP server called NAME, with its tests.

agentlib new mcp [OPTIONS] NAME
FlagDefaultMeaning
--server-idnoneThe server's ID in the tool registry.
--descriptionnoneOne line on what the server offers.
--portnoneLocal HTTP port.
--no-pinoffDo not pin the tools' input schemas now.
--forceoffOverwrite files that exist and differ.
--from-csvnonePropose the tools from the CSV files in this folder, and copy the files in.
--from-openapinonePropose the tools from the GET operations of this OpenAPI 3 document.
--base-urlnoneWhere the API is. Default: the document's.

Generated service commands and HTTP endpoints
Command or endpointPurpose
"%PYTHON%" -m helper "Say hello" --thread demoAsk one question. The default thread is default.
"%PYTHON%" -m ai_agent_lib_cli run helperServe the agent over HTTP. Defaults to 127.0.0.1 and the generated port, initially 8000. Accepts --host and --port.
"%PYTHON%" -m ai_agent_lib_cli run directoryServe MCP over Streamable HTTP at /mcp. The first generated server uses port 8100.
GET /healthzLiveness: is the HTTP listener responding?
GET /readyzReadiness: are services and graph preparation complete?
POST /invokeAccepts {"input":{"question":"..."},"thread_id":"..."} for the generated agent. Returns output, thread_id, and request_id.
POST /invoke with Accept: text/event-streamWith live_updates=True in agent_app, streams provisional model text, then an accepted result with token usage. Enabled in newly generated agents and rmprep.
POST /invoke/streamThe same input, with graph-step updates as server-sent events. Each event reports a completed graph update.

For authenticated requests, send Authorization: Bearer <token>. An optional x-request-id correlates requests. The local static identity supplies the tutorial's configured development caller.

Agent Lab shows a live draft while the model responds. It removes the temporary draft panel once the final outcome is saved, then shows input/output tokens, elapsed time and cache-hit ratio when reported. Usage includes model calls made for tool selection and revisions. Missing counts display as unavailable; fake-model usage is marked simulated. Reopening a conversation restores its saved answer and metrics.

The default pattern guardrails check the output size before each live text update. Blocking PII checks and structured-output schemas wait for the complete response before releasing text. Live drafts are provisional; only the accepted final answer is saved. Chat keeps metrics and the Phoenix or Langfuse trace link visible, with detailed evidence available through the trace and Logs page.

In the MCP console, each admitted named query writes a data_query line: query name, duration, returned rows and columns, truncation and masked columns. Local detail logging also shows bounded, credential-masked parameters such as client UEN, date range and page offset. Returned records are not copied into these log lines. Deployed logging omits parameter values; use the request ID to connect queries with the MCP call and model trace.

The optional library Langfuse integration adds an Open trace in Langfuse link to each accepted response. Langfuse runs as a separate service; developers connect with the existing Python and pip setup. Each request has its own trace, grouped with the thread's other requests. Model attempts and MCP calls appear in its timeline. Checkpoint IDs link back to saved state inspected through the agent. Content export is an explicit setting; operational metrics retain their existing destination.

Checkpoint reference collection stops after one second or 64 references. If the history read times out, the answer still returns and trace metadata marks the references unavailable. The checkpoint database remains the source of saved conversation state.

Newly generated agents include this integration in service.py. The library owns export and shutdown; your response function owns what the graph does. This is dependency injection: tests supply an in-memory exporter, and deployed services use the same graph with the configured exporter. Existing graph callbacks are preserved, and governed native tools appear once in the trace. The adapter adds output.trace when enabled; existing answer, streaming and checkpoint interfaces keep their behavior.

Get the project URL and keys from the platform team, then put them in a private settings file. From Command Prompt, select the agent's Python environment and follow its generated docs/langfuse.md:

set "EAP_LANGFUSE_ENV_FILE=F:\work\langfuse\agent.env"
python -m your_agent.service

Replace the path and module name with your own values. The file sets EAP_LANGFUSE_ENABLED=true and the project settings listed in the configuration table. EAP_LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=false records metadata and usage; set it to true for approved test data to inspect messages and results. The generated dependencies include the otel extra and install with Python and pip. For an older service, follow the integration steps. The verified rmprep walkthrough shows a memo and follow-ups with their MCP calls, token counts and checkpoint references.

For a desktop trial using Python and pip, follow the local Phoenix walkthrough. Run start-phoenix.bat setup once, then enable Phoenix in the root .env. Run start-local.bat to start the local Phoenix server before the MCP, agent, and UI services. It keeps separate .venv packages and uses the default Python; stop-local.bat stops the stack and preserves SQLite traces. The agent adds an Open trace in Agent Lab link to each response, opening the configured Phoenix trace. The walkthrough lists the opt-in settings and a verified Anthropic conversation. Enable one tracing backend at a time. Existing Langfuse integrations remain supported.

Blocking PII checks and structured-output schemas buffer text until they pass. Default pattern checks validate each growing text update, allowing early display. Drafts can still change during business validation; only the final accepted answer enters chat history. Keep live_updates=False when application-specific checks must finish before any draft is shown.

Long chats load recent messages first; use View older messages to browse earlier pages. Reopening a held thread checks the agent's outcome journal without resending its question. A confirmed outcome restores the answer or failure; an unknown outcome keeps the thread held. Local rmprep and newly generated local agents save this journal in .agentlib/outcomes.sqlite beside their project file. It contains accepted answers, so protect it like checkpoints. Restart the agent and UI after updating their code.

The agent HTTP service accepts one active request per caller and thread. An overlapping request receives 409 thread_busy before it runs. Wait for the active turn to finish before submitting again. The default guard covers one application instance. Multiple worker processes or replicas need a shared admission provider; a shared checkpoint database alone does not serialize turns. See thread admission for deployment and extension details.

Expected library error types

Catch errors by type and inspect their diagnostic fields: expected, actual, and fix. Include the full traceback when reporting unexpected exceptions.

ErrorMeaningNext action
ConfigurationErrorA setting or adapter configuration is invalid.Fix configuration and rerun diagnostics.
PolicyDeniedIdentity, policy, an entitlement, or a guardrail refused the action.Inspect the reason and resolve the permission or input problem before retrying.
ValidationFailedData does not match the expected schema.Handle invalid input or output explicitly.
TransientErrorA timeout, throttling response, or temporary service failure remains after configured retries.Consider a bounded retry with delay if the operation is safe to repeat.
IntegrityErrorAn audit write, hash, or schema pin check failed.Investigate the underlying failure or interface mismatch.
CredentialsExpiredErrorA credential or session expired.Refresh credentials through the approved sign-in flow.
BudgetExceededThe request reached a call or token limit.Inspect loops and request size before changing limits.

The exported ExecutionPaused type is reserved for planned pause support; see release scope for its status.
